title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour
location: Unique Lancaster, 23 N Walnut Street, Lancaster, 17603, United States
description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally! 


Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century. 


Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI. 


But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region. 


As you explore, you’ll stop at five handpicked local spots to enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring hearty breakfast sandwiches, fresh fruits, sweet pastries, and other morning favorites. 


Please note: This tour offers vegetarian-friendly options only. If you have other dietary needs, we recommend our International Food Tour for a better fit. 


Whether you’re passionate about history, love discovering new flavors, or just want a memorable way to see the city, the Lancaster History & Breakfast Tour is a great choice for solo explorers, couples, and groups alike.

title: Valley Forge Park River Trail (Pawlings Rd)
description:
Walking Tails
Directions: From the intersection of Egypt Road and Park Ave./Pawlings Road, proceed on Pawlings Road heading towards the Schuylkill River. You will pass Mill Grove on your right, St. Gabriel Hall on your left and Pawling Farm on your left. You are getting close when you pass Sullivan Blvd. on your left and Gertrude St. on your right. You turn left on the next and last left (right before you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River). Look for the River Trail Valley Forge Park sign visible from Pawlings Road. The gravel parking lot is straight ahead and also visible from Pawlings Road. If you go over the bridge over the Schuylkill River, you have gone too far and are now in Chester county.

CLICK DIRECTLY ON THE MAP IF YOU THINK YOU ARE LOST. IT WILL BRING YOU RIGHT TO US WHERE WE MEET.

This walk goes out about 1.5 miles along the Schuylkill River and then we come back the way we came, for a total of 3 miles. This is a dirt/gravel/mulch trail through the woods.

Start Time: Arrive a few minutes early. We will start hiking promptly at the scheduled time.

Duration of the walk – depends on the people and dogs in the group. We frequently end up walking in smaller packs based on the comfort level of the participants.

In the past this walk takes a little over an hour.

Please remember pooh bags and that your dog must be on a leash that is no more than 10 feet long. Sturdy shoes or hiking boots are recommended. Dress appropriately for weather conditions.

NOTICE: By attending this event you are agreeing that YOU ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR YOUR OWN SAFETY AT ALL TIMES. The hike leader and other members cannot be held responsible for any damages, accidents, or liabilities incurred while hiking with us.

Valley Forge Trail Map (http://www.nps.gov/vafo/planyourvisit/maps.htm)

title: Children's Chapel
location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. 
After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. 
The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. 
Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.

title: My Generation Tour at American Music Theatre
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Highway East, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
My Generation Tour: The Lovin Spoonful, Terry Sylvester and Gary Lewis & The Playboys
“This good-time spectacular celebrates the time of our lives with all three acts performing with their own full bands spanning the golden singles-era of pop music, from 1965 to 1975. This was the magic time where hit singles ruled the charts and won our hearts,” producer Jim Della Croce exclaims. Terry Sylvester, who famously replaced Graham Nash after he left The Hollies, will perform along with famed pop legend Gary Lewis. “This show is the baby-boomer bucket list must see event of the year, a hip trip back to the era that defined our generation,” he concludes. 
Between The Lovin’ Spoonful, The Hollies, and Gary Lewis and The Playboys, the charts exploded every week with a new tune that captivated our rock and roll souls. Nearly 30 hits will explode throughout this two-hour celebration: “Daydream,” “Do You Believe in Magic,” “This Diamond Ring,” “Carrie Anne,” “Long Cool Woman (in a Black Dress), “Count Me In,” “He Ain’t Heavy, He’s My Brother,” “Summer in the City,” “She’s Just My Style,” “You Didn’t Have to Be So Nice,” “On a Carousel,”  “Sure Gonna Miss Her” and “The Air that I Breathe.”

Enjoy a 5-star Lancaster County ice cream tour experience with Strasburg Scooter Tours. You’ll see rolling farmlands, pass by horse and buggies, and enjoy some of the best Ice Cream in Lancaster County! It’s a stark contrast to the usual fast-paced and congested areas of larger cities. For those craving something different or one of the best romantic date night ideas, join us! 
We designed this tour to be an experience you can share with someone. We’ll only use Scoot Coupes, so single riders will have to look for someone to bring on the tour. It will be well worth it as you can expect exceptional views. Bond throughout the experience alongside our expert guide and relish some tasty ice cream* as we Ride around the rolling farmland surrounding the Village of Intercourse and Bird-in-Hand, PA. 
>> Check Out Our Ice Cream Tour in Strasburg, PA 
Itinerary
Some of our past tours have included: 

An evening drive through PA Dutch Country
Beautiful rolling farm-scapes and off-the-beaten-path adventures
A stop at one of the best ice cream shops that Amish Country has to offer*

And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! 
*Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.

title: Asking the Hard Questions
location: Church of the Apostles UCC, 1850 Marietta Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
At Church of the Apostles, we know many are carrying deep and honest questions about faith, especially in light of what is happening in our country and throughout the world. Questions like “Where is God in all of this?” are not signs of weak faith, but part of a faithful journey we are called to walk together. 
To create space for these conversations, we invite you to a new monthly series, Asking the Hard Questions, hosted by our seminary intern, Deklan Lewis, in the Parlor. Together, we will explore doubt, struggle, and belief as meaningful parts of discipleship. Our first two gatherings will include viewing and discussing the film God on Trial as we wrestle, much like Jacob, with faith and what it means to follow Jesus today. 
To accommodate different schedules, two sessions will be offered each month: Monday morning, April 27th at 10 AM, and Thursday evening, April 30th at 6 PM. All are welcome to join this thoughtful, open, and supportive conversation.

description:

For Teens ages 13-18 years of age only.Calling all teen readers! Join us for Teen Book Talk, a fun and engaging monthly book discussion group led by members of our Teen Advisory Board! Book selections are chosen by teens during advisory meetings. Interested in joining the Teen Advisory Board? Sign up through the library calendar. Each month, we’ll dive into a new title—ranging from trending young adult fiction to graphic novels, fantasy epics, thought-provoking contemporary stories, and more.This month we'll be reading "A Little Princess" by Frances Hodgson. Sara Crewe looks like a princess as she enters boarding school - she wears beautiful clothes and has the best manners.  But what happens when all of the money disappears and Sara is left with nothing?  She is forced to sleep in the attic of the school and is wearing rags.  Can Sara overcome this "riches to rags" turn of events and come out as the princess she knows she is in the end? location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Ignatian Spirituality
location: Saint James Parish House Library
description:
Ignatian Spirituality
Tuesday evenings from 5:15 – 6:15 PM
September 9 – April 28, 2026
Ignatian spirituality is a way of living spirituality in everyday life. It asserts that God is present in our world and actively involved in our lives. It is a pathway to deeper prayer, good decisions guided by keen discernment and an active life of service to others. 
This 34-week program is designed for individuals who wish to commit to personal transformation by encountering God and deepening their experience of the divine. It will involve a daily and weekly commitment to spiritual practices with help and support from spiritual director Pat Latshaw. 
The book, The Ignatian Adventure by Kevin O’Brien will be used for discussion and to guide the group’s approach to spiritual growth with techniques that have been in use for almost 500 years. 
The cost is $875 for 34 sessions. Scholarships are available. 
Have questions about scholarships and/or Ignatian Spirituality? Click here to email Pat Latshaw.

title: Phil's Hills: Groffdale Repeats
description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup
**Ride Leader:** Phil Newswanger

**Phil’s Hills**: a series of structured hill repeat rides designed to build strength, endurance and boost your overall fitness.

**Cue and GPX link:** [Phil's Hills: Groffdale Repeats](https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53989662)

What to Expect:

* **Route:** Expect a total distance of approximately **15-20 miles**, including **3-4 loops** of a circuit featuring **1-2 climbing segment**.
* **Focus:** We'll emphasize maintaining a consistent climbing tempo, active recovery between efforts, and repeating the effort to build power and efficiency.
* **Pace:** We'll maintain a comfortable average pace range of **14-16 mph**.
* **No-Drop Policy:** You'll never be left behind! We'll regroup after climbs to ensure everyone stays together.

\-\-\-

Helmets are mandatory. No earbuds or audible music-playing devices. Please bring water, and a basic repair kit (spare tube, tire levers, pump/CO2 inflator).

title: Lit Lovers Book Group
location: Milanof-Schock, MJY Grissinger Board Room
description:
Book Club, Adults

Lit Lovers is an eclectic reading group with a primary focus on fiction, while also exploring memoirs, short stories, biographies and autobiographies, mysteries, science fiction, and select works of nonfiction. The group is known for its lively, thoughtful discussions and makes a concerted effort to respect differing viewpoints. To keep conversations focused and meaningful, social chatter, gossip, and romance novels are generally kept outside the allotted discussion time.Lit Lovers gravitate toward modern fiction distinguished by strong writing, well-developed characters, and compelling narratives. Common themes include contemporary issues, family conflict, and the triumph of the human spirit, with a healthy appreciation for humor. Members read for both personal enrichment and enjoyment, and the group frequently selects works by international authors, books set abroad, or stories that explore multicultural perspectives.For a list of this year's book selections, click on the photo to the left or pick up a bookmark at the library!

location: Saint James Episcopal Church, 103 North Duke Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Evening Compline
via Zoom
Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: The American Revolution and Mennonites: A Crisis of Conscience
location: Historic Rock Ford, 881 Rockford Road, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Historic Rock Ford’s Untold Stories of the Revolution Lecture Series welcomes Kenneth Sensenig as he presents “The American Revolution and Mennonites: A Crisis of Conscience.” In 1777, during the defense of Philadelphia, the peaceful Ephrata Cloister became an unlikely battlefield of conscience as wounded soldiers were brought there for nursing. Join us for an exploration of the story of John and Anna Baer, Mennonite pacifists who faced an impossible dilemma: how to care for wounded soldiers whose cause contradicted their deepest beliefs.  



Christa Mylin from Mennonite Life will also be assisting with this lecture regarding material artifacts that will be on display at the end of the lecture. There will also be a Q&A session. 



This presentation will take place in the Langmuir Education Room on the first floor of the Rock Ford Barn. Admission is for the lecture only and does not include the Snyder Gallery or Hand Mansion.

Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.) 

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

title: Leslie Odom, Jr.
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $79 $99 $109 $129
 
Leslie Odom, Jr. is a Tony and Grammy Award-winning, three-time Emmy and two-time Academy Award-nominated songwriter, actor, and a New York Times bestselling author. Well known for his breakout role as ‘Aaron Burr’ in the Pulitzer Prize-winning Broadway musical Hamilton, Odom made the season’s most highly anticipated return to his award-winning role in September 2025. During his limited engagement run, which came nine years after his final bow, Hamilton hit its highest ever gross in its ten years on Broadway. 
Odom’s long-awaited return to Broadway following his original Hamilton run came in 2023 as a producer, alongside his beloved Nicolette Robinson and the gracious Jeffrey Richards, with the classic American comedy Purlie Victorious: A Non-Confederate Romp Through the Cotton Patch written by the legendary Ossie Davis. The revival opened to widespread critical acclaim. Odom was Tony-nominated for his performance, and the production received six nominations and one win. Purlie Victorious was recorded and aired as part of PBS’ Great Performances.  
Odom has continued to captivate audiences across film and television including his star turn as legendary soul singer Sam Cooke in the Amazon film adaptation of One Night in Miami…, directed by Regina King. His lauded portrayal of the soul icon and musical performance of original song “Speak Now” earned him multiple awards and nominations. Additional film and television credits include Rian Johnson’s record-breaking 2022 Knives Out sequel, Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery, for Netflix, The Many Saints of Newark, a prequel to David Chase’s award-winning HBO series The Sopranos, Apple TV+’s Central Park (2020 Emmy nomination), Hamilton on Disney+ (2021 Emmy nomination), host of “The Tony Awards Present: Broadway’s Back!” on CBS (2022 Emmy nomination), Abbott Elementary, The Proud Family: Louder and Prouder, Harriet, and many more. 
In March 2018, Odom added the title of author to his resume with the release of his book – Failing Up: How to Take Risks, Aim Higher and Never Stop Learning, which was recently released in paperback in March 2025. Co-written with Nicolette Robinson, Odom’s first children’s book, I Love You More Than You’ll Ever Know, was published by Feiwel & Friends in March 2023. The book debuted on the New York Times bestseller list at #7 in its first week. Odom has released six full-length albums. His sixth and first-ever live album, An Offering: Live at Speakeasy Studios, was released on October 17, 2025.

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near. 

The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls. 

People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

The eight-member troupe uses everything but conventional percussion instruments – matchboxes, wooden poles, brooms, garbage cans, Zippo lighters, hubcaps – to fill the stage with magnificent rhythms.  The return of the percussive hit also brings some new surprises, with some sections of the show now updated and restructured and the addition of two new full-scale routines, utilizing props like tractor tire inner tubes and paint cans.  As USA Today says, “STOMP finds beautiful noises in the strangest places.”  STOMP.  See what all the noise is about.

RSVP Today










Innovative exhibits, created with leading historians and designers, confront slavery, freedom, and the ongoing fight for equality in America. LancasterHistory—together with many collaborative partners—are eager to welcome the public for this once-in-a-generation moment for our community, a celebration as bold as the history it honors! 



The excitement kicks off Friday morning as we officially open the Stevens & Smith Center with a celebratory ribbon-cutting! Doors open at 8am for coffee, light fare, and mingling. America 250 programming is sponsored by a generous donation from The Friends of Adamstown Area LibraryAnn Dapice received a PhD in psychology, sociology and philosophy from the University of Pennsylvania. title: Mako & Haejin Fujimura
location: The Trust Performing Arts Center, 37 N. Market St., Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Sponsored by The Open Discourse Coalition, this special evening at The Trust welcomes back Makoto Fujimura, accompanied by his wife, Haejin Fujimura, for a conversation centered on their forthcoming book, “Beauty X Justice.” 
We often imagine beauty and justice as opposites: one concerned with truth and fairness, the other with aesthetics and adornment. What if they aren’t rivals at all? What if beauty and justice belong together, moving in step to create lives, communities, and cultures marked by courage and abundance? 
In this fireside-style conversation, the Fujimuras will explore how beauty and justice can work hand in hand, drawing from their shared life, creative practice, and public work. More than ideas alone, this evening offers a close look at how their vision takes shape in the real world, through art, advocacy, and cultural renewal. 
The conversation will be guided by The Trust’s Founder & Curator, Tom Becker, beneath the Beaux Arts vaulted ceiling of The Trust Performing Arts Center in downtown Lancaster. 
Bring your friends, your curiosity, and your questions. Seating is free with advanced registration. Space is limited, so reserve your tickets early!

title: Living the Experience: An Underground Railroad Reenactment & Interactive Experience
location: Bethel AME Church Culutral Center, 512 E. Strawberry Street, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
One of Lancaster County’s most moving and powerfully significant hidden gems, Living the Experience is a creative, spiritual, and interactive historical reenactment of the Underground Railroad, at the Historical Bethel African Methodist Episcopal Church in the City of Lancaster. Living The Experience (LTE) is the first Underground Railroad reenactment in Central Pennsylvania made available with a regular schedule of performances. It has been presented to groups from all over the nation, and as far away as Australia, Alaska, Africa, and Europe.

This Underground Railroad living history program is presented interactively in first person interpretation in an effort to bring alive the people, places, and events of Lancaster County. The program actively engages its audiences in the learning of Lancaster’s involvement in the Underground Railroad and also its involvement as a free community of Africans.

Those who attend are provided an honest portrayal of the experiential realities of those involved in the Underground Railroad and how relevant the history is in these current times. From the stories that are told, the spirituals that are sung, and in the emotional connections that are felt, people are provided an opportunity to learn and to gain a clearer perspective on the events and the people involved.  Following the reenactment, a southern style meal is served, and local vendors are on site. For 28 years, this story has been told as we would love to make it yours! Step into history like never before. Come live the experience!

location: Historic Rock Ford, 881 Rockford Road, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Historic Rock Ford’s America250 Lecture Series presents “Valley Forge Celebrates the French Alliance” by Nancy K. Loane, Ed.D.  



May 6, 1778 was a beautiful day for a celebration at the Valley Forge encampment. The alliance between France and the United States of America, important in supplying vital military and financial aid to the new country, had just been ratified. Now, Washington’s soldiers could hope that the war would soon be over, the Continental Army would disband, and they would go home.  



This presentation will begin at 2 PM in the Langmuir Education Room located on the first floor of the Rock Ford Barn. Prior to the lecture, attendees may visit the Snyder Gallery and our 2026 Focus Exhibit. The Snyder Gallery closes at 4 PM.

title: SOUL & SPIRIT A Gospel • Jazz • Spoken Word Experience
location: First Reformed Church, 40 East Orange Street, Lancaster, Pennsylvania, 17602, United States
description:
First Reformed Church of Lancaster will present Soul & Spirit, a sacred arts experience celebrating Black history, faith, resilience, justice, and hope through Gospel music, Jazz, and the Spoken Word on Sunday, May 3 at 4 PM in their historic 1854 sanctuary at 40 E. Orange Street in downtown Lancaster.  Soul & Spirit is not a traditional concert—it is worship through art. Through sound and story, the program honors the past, speaks truth to the present, and imagines a hopeful future. Originally scheduled in February to honor Black History month, the event was postponed due to winter storms.  
Hosted by Dr. Dominique Denman, Soul & Spirit invites the community into a meaningful Black History Month celebration rooted in faith, creativity, and collective memory.  The program also features Dr. Kellie Turner, and Ms. Alanna Piper.
All are warmly invited to experience Soul & Spirit where you can expect a 90-minute curated sacred arts program of Gospel music, Jazz, and Spoken Word performances, a welcoming, reflective, and celebratory atmosphere with a diverse audience from across the Lancaster community.
Come as you are. Bring your spirit.  Leave inspired.
This event is free and open to the public. A freewill offering will be received during the program to support the ongoing care, repair, and sustainability of First Reformed Lancaster’s historic sacred space.

title: The Painter's Fire
location: Historic Rock Ford, 881 Rockford Road, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Historic Rock Ford’s Untold Stories Series welcomes author Zara Anishanslin as she presents a lecture on her book “The Painter’s Fire: A Forgotten History of the Artists Who Championed the American Revolution.”  



Artists played a crucial role in the American Revolution, focusing on three figures: Robert Edge Pine, Prince Demah, and Patience Wright. Her book argues that art was a powerful tool for forging revolutionary ideals, highlighting how these diverse artists—including a woman and an enslaved man—used paint, canvas, and wax to support the cause of liberty on both sides of the Atlantic.  



A limited number of copies of the author’s book will be available for purchase and signing following the lecture. 



This lecture will be held in the Langmuir Education Room on the first floor of the Rock Ford Barn. Admission is for the lecture only and does not include the Snyder Gallery or Hand Mansion.

description:

This immersive evening invites guests to experience food, art, and music through thoughtfully curated sensory stations, each representing a Touchstone program and the impact it creates for youth in our community. 



Guests will enjoy seasonal cuisine, interactive experiences, a silent and live auction, and powerful stories of impact from students and families served through Touchstone’s programs, including mental health access assistance, mentorship through Rise Above, student career exploration, and clinical fellowships. 



Proceeds from the evening help remove financial barriers to therapy, connect youth with trusted mentors, and support the next generation of mental health professionals serving Lancaster County. 



Join us for an unforgettable evening that engages the senses and supports a mission that changes lives.

title: Leonid & Friends
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $44 $54 $64 $74
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, September 24, 2025 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, September 26, 2025 at 10:00 a.m. 
With multiple sold-out U.S. tours under its belt and hundreds of thousands of fans around the world, Leonid & Friends continues to astound its global audience with its unique ability in capturing the spirit, musicality, and fire of American supergroup Chicago. 
And what is even more stunning is that Leonid & Friends, comprised of 11 of the finest musicians in Russia, haven’t seen Chicago perform live until recently, yet replicates the band’s complex arrangements amazingly note for note. Chicago has never been in Russia, and none of us have attended their concerts until just recently in the United States,” said Leonid Vorobyev, a multi-instrumentalist who is the band’s leader. “We have only recordings and videos (to help us learn Chicago songs).” 
Ironically, Vorobyev wasn’t always a fan of horn bands, and as a teenager gravitated to the hard-driving guitar-based sounds of the Beatles, Creedence Clearwater Revival, Deep Purple, and Grand Funk Railroad. “In the early 1970s in the USSR, electric guitars, amplifiers, and drums were rare to find so at school we were playing self-made instruments,” Vorobyev explained. “We were allowed to rehearse in the same room with a horns band. Those musicians almost always were drunk and quite often tried to play with us our rock songs. It was a nightmare, and I hated them all!” 
But that all changed when Vorobyev heard Chicago. He became an instant fan. “I loved so much the brilliant mixture of rock guitars, drums, and jazz horns with bright vocal harmonies,” he said.
In 2014, Vorobyev decided to indulge his love for the band by gathering a few fellow musicians in a studio to record a video of them playing his favorite Chicago tune, Brand New Love Affair. No charts or scores of the song existed so Vorobyev transcribed the tune by ear. The result was a YouTube video that quickly went viral. Since then Leonid & Friends has recorded videos of other Chicago hits including Make Me Smile, 25 or 6 to 4, and Saturday In The Park. 
All total the videos have received more than 50 million views. Also, Leonid & Friends has recorded two albums showcasing its tribute to Chicago. In September of 2018, the band recorded its first song from legendary supergroup Earth, Wind, & Fire and also paid tribute to the band Blood, Sweat & Tears as well. 
Borrowing a line from one of Chicago’s biggest hits, “it’s only the beginning” of great things from Leonid & Friends.

Herman’s Hermits
British Invasion icon Peter Noone—the unmistakable voice of Herman’s Hermits—brings a hit-packed evening of songs, stories, and good-natured humor. Backed by his seasoned band, Noone revisits the soundtrack of the 1960s with favorites like “I’m Into Something Good,” “Mrs. Brown, You’ve Got a Lovely Daughter,” “There’s a Kind of Hush,” “I’m Henry VIII, I Am,” “Silhouettes,” and more. Contemporary crooner Chris Ruggiero brings the spirit of the ’60s and ’70s to life in a shimmering, feel-good concert of timeless pop. Backed by a crack band and lush arrangements, Chris leans into the romance, rhythm, and melody of the era, delivering fresh takes that honor the originals while letting his smooth, soaring vocals shine. Sing along to favorites like “This Magic Moment,” “My Cherie Amour,” “More Today Than Yesterday,” “Unchained Melody,” “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” and more—interwoven with charming stories about the artists and the songs that shaped a generation. With easy charisma, crisp harmonies, and plenty of heart, Ruggiero turns nostalgia into a living, breathing celebration—perfect for date night, family night, or anyone who loves great songs sung beautifully. If you treasure classic pop and soul, this uplifting evening will leave you smiling long after the final note.

location: Ephrata, EPH 1/2 Multipurpose Room Kitchen Side
description:

Oh Captain, My Captain! is a short form worldbuilding role-playing game (RPG) that explores heroism and the complicated relationships we have with people we admire. The game revolves around players drawing from a deck of cards with open-ended questions. Each question players answer helps them learn about their character, their world, their captain and the complicated relationship they have with a living legend. Players use these answers to make connections between their stories leading up one of three final questions that end the game. No experience or prep needed! Ages 10-12.

The Commonwealth Monument Project returns to the Lancaster Public Library for its annual LIVE AND LEARN CHAUTAUQUA.Presented in memory of the life and legacy of Lenwood Sloan, the 2026 series is a salute to PA Abolitionist William Whipper's galvanizing Reading Society. Five famous speeches presented by colleagues of Whipper are matched to five contemporary books selected by the library staff. ➡️ Read the book prior to the meeting, then we'll listen to the corresponding speech and discuss both during our gathering.Registration is helpful, but walk-ins will not be turned away.List of books:January 13 - Black Genius: Essays on an American Legacy by Tre JohnsonFebruary 10 - The New Jim Crow: Mass Incarceration in the Age of Colorblindness by Michelle Alexander March 10 - Misbehaving at the Crossroads by Honoree Fanonne Jeffers April 14 - Between the World and Me by Ta-Nehisi Coates May 12 - Citizen: An American Lyric by Claudia Rankine List of speeches:January 13 - David Walker, 1829 - Appeal to the Colored Citizens of the World!February 10 - William Whipper, 1834 - The Slavery of IntemperanceMarch 10 - Henry Highland Garnett, 1843 - Call to RebellionApril 14 - Thomas Morris Chester, 1862 - Negro Self Respect and Pride of RaceMay 12 - Frederick Douglass, 1894 - Lessons of the Hour

title: Farm to Fork Experience
location: Bird-in-Hand Village Inn & Suites, 2695 Old Philadelphia Pike, Bird-in-Hand, PA, 17505, United States
description:
Real Farms • Real Food
May 13, 2026
Food doesn’t get any more authentic than Bird-in-Hand’s Farm-to-Fork Experience. From milking cows to making ice cream to growing chemical-free produce from seed, you’ll meet Mennonite and Amish farmers and get an intimate view of how Lancaster County’s bounty begins. Our own John Smucker, an eighth-generation farmer, will be your guide on this unforgettable experience, which culminates in a mouth-watering farm-to-fork meal. 
The Farm to Fork Experience package includes:
• Two-night stay in the historic Bird-in-Hand Village Inn & Suites
• Tours of local farms and a lunch made with ingredients from our tour – see itinerary below
• Daily deluxe continental breakfasts for two at the Village Inn & Suites or credit at the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe
• Dinner for two at the Bird-in-Hand Family Restaurant & Smorgasbord on Tuesday or Wednesday
• Welcome market basket filled with local foods 
Space is limited so reserve early. Enjoy this package for $585 (plus tax). Extend your stay for only $109 a night (plus tax). For more information on the Village Inn & Suites, click here. Walking is required for these tours. 
Requires $200 deposit to reserve your tour (refundable up to two weeks prior to event). $109 extra night available for any room type. Taxes not included. 
  
2026 TOUR ITINERARY 
Rise, Shine & Dine (5:30 am): Wake up with the roosters and see cows being milked at our neighbor Aaron Lantz’s organic farm. Then savor a delicious farm-fresh breakfast with the Lantz family in their kitchen. 
Hydroponic Farming: At Millcreek Hydroponics, we’ll learn about the sustainable year-round growing methods for their lettuce and microgreens, and tour their greenhouse. 
The Time is Ripe: Take an orchard tour of Kauffman’s Fruit & Farm Market and learn how they produce their apple cider. 
Veggies on the Vine: Amish farmer Ephraim Huyard will show us his biological methods of growing plants, and how he grows the chemical-free vegetable plants. 
Growing Green: Meet Wesley Groff, third-generation farmer of Groff’s Celery and Vegetable Farm, and learn how he grows crops from seed in a chemical-free environment. 
Grown Local Luncheon: You’ve seen where it’s grown. Now taste the fresh difference. Receive a market basket of local foods after lunch. 
Save Room for Dessert: Our last stop after lunch will be a visit to the Bird-in-Hand Bakery & Cafe, where we make our artisan ice cream.

title: Gary Allan with guest Mark Mackay
location: PA, United States
description:
Tickets: $69 $79 $89 $99 
With the allure of a modern day outlaw, Gary Allan has won over fans, peers, and critics with his signature blend of smoldering vocals, rebellious lyrics, and raucous live performances. While becoming a force on the country music scene, Allan has remained true to his artistic voice each step of the way. The California native has released nine studio albums selling over 8 million albums, been certified platinum on three back-to-back albums, and been certified gold five times. Allan has five #1 hits on country radio and fourteen Top 10 hits to his credit. He has amassed over 2.8 billion total streams and has debuted at #1 on the Billboard Country Album chart four times, along with his SET YOU FREE album debuting at the top of the Billboard 200 (Pop Chart). He is described as “dark and dreamy” in Entertainment Weekly and deemed a “maverick” by Rolling Stone.  He sells out venues as a headliner from NY to LA and has appeared on The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, Late Show with David Letterman, Late Night with Jimmy Fallon, Live with Kelly and Michael, and Jimmy Kimmel Live. He has also landed on the covers of Country Weekly, Pollstar, and People magazine. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
May 30, June 13, June 27, July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

title: Dick Fox’s Golden Boys starring Frankie Avalon and Fabian with special guest Tommy Cono Tributing Bobby Rydell
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $69 $79 $89 $99 
Relive the magic of the golden era of rock ‘n’ roll with Dick Fox’s Golden Boys! This unforgettable concert event reunites beloved teen idols of the late 1950s and early 1960s — Frankie Avalon and Fabian, with special guest Tommy Cono (tributing Bobby Rydell) — for an evening packed with timeless hits, charm, and nostalgia. 
From Avalon’s chart-topping favorites like “Venus” and “Why” to Fabian’s energetic classics including “Turn Me Loose” and “Tiger,” audiences will be transported back to a time when rock ‘n’ roll ruled the airwaves. With the addition of Tommy Cono’s smooth vocals and dynamic stage presence, this show is a celebration of music that defined a generation. 
Dick Fox’s Golden Boys blends unforgettable songs, stories, and humor into a joyful trip down memory lane — reminding us why these performers became household names and fan favorites around the world. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

Let's get digging! 💎🏺

In this engaging and informative session, Barb Bingham, Community Engagement and Training Specialist, will share insight into how human trafficking affects our communities and what we can do to address it. The presentation is designed to raise awareness, increase identification, and empower attendees to recognize and respond to trafficking situations safely and effectively. Whether you're a concerned citizen, community leader or frontline professional, this session will provide practical tools and a deeper understanding of this critical issue. Learn the signs. Understand the impact. Be part of the solution. Ages 18+.

Super groups have a prestigious history in the music industry from such legendary rockers as The Traveling Wilburys to the iconic country foursome The Highwaymen to the stellar trio of Dolly Parton, Emmylou Harris, and Linda Ronstadt.  There’s a special excitement when successful artists combine their individual talents and star power to create something fresh and exciting.  That tradition continues with Brothers Of The Heart – Jimmy Fortune, Bradley Walker, Mike Rogers, and Ben Isaacs – who reimagine country, gospel, and pop classics with their renditions of iconic songs such as “Ring of Fire,” “Desperado,” “Bye Bye Love,” “Precious Memories,” and more. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Registration RequestedCortney Dean is a Conservation Biologist and Independent Researcher living in Northern Wisconsin. title: Mocktails & Meaning™: Behind the Scenes of Human Trafficking
location: Church of the Apostles UCC, 1850 Marietta Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17603, United States
description:
Join us for our May 21, 2026 Mocktails & Meaning™ gathering for a powerful and eye-opening conversation led by Brad Ortenzi, Eastern USA Regional Director of ZOE International and Coordinator of the Berks and Lancaster County Human Trafficking Task Forces. Drawing on his experience as a former Ephrata Police Detective, his work with federal and county child exploitation task forces, and his international work combating trafficking in Thailand, Brad will take us behind the scenes of human trafficking in Lancaster County. This session will explore how traffickers recruit and control victims, the psychological realities of trauma bonding, and how local task forces respond through both enforcement and prevention. Time will be set aside for questions and dialogue. We’ll be serving a Mai Tai Mocktail as we engage this important and impactful conversation.

description:

Pizza is provided free upstairs. Beer/wine/soda/etc at the bar downstairs!

This months speakers:
**Luke Westfall - *Actually… it IS rocket science ***
At some point, every Kerbal engineer gets tired of manually throttling up and watching their rocket cartwheel into the ocean. In this talk, we'll use Kerbal Space Program, a beloved space flight simulator where failure is half the fun, as a playground for exploring two approaches to automation: the onboard scripting of kOS and the external control API of kRPC. Along the way, we'll discover what they can teach us about flight dynamics, control loops, and why sometimes the best debugging session involves a tiny green astronaut.

**Ken Richards - *Walk Up Song ***
Come see if Ken’s app can guess your age and pick a song you’ll vibe to. Then stick around — he’ll share the creative story, lessons on large vs. small models, and where AI can fall short.

title: Lee Brice with special guest Payton Smith
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $99 $109 $119 $139
 
Get ready for an unforgettable night of country music when Lee Brice takes the stage at American Music Theatre! Known for his powerhouse vocals, heartfelt storytelling, and chart-topping hits like “Hard to Love,” “I Don’t Dance,” “One of Them Girls,” and “Rumor,” Brice delivers a show packed with energy, emotion, and authenticity. 
A multi-platinum artist, songwriter, and CMA award-winner, Lee Brice brings together the raw honesty of classic country with a modern edge that resonates with fans of all ages. Whether he’s performing tender ballads or high-energy anthems, his passion and stage presence make every song hit home. 
Rising country artist Payton Smith brings a fresh, heartfelt sound to the stage—blending modern country energy with the storytelling roots that define the genre. Hailing from Louisiana, Smith has quickly made a name for himself with his smooth vocals, relatable lyrics, and a style that bridges classic influences with today’s country sound. 
Since breaking onto the scene, he’s earned attention from fans and industry alike, touring with major acts and releasing songs that capture everything from young love to life on the road. With a mix of infectious melodies and genuine emotion, Smith delivers a live show that feels both intimate and high-energy. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
June 13, June 27, July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

Get ready to relive the soundtrack of the late ’70s and ’80s when Lou Gramm, the legendary original lead singer of Foreigner, takes the stage at American Music Theatre! With one of rock’s most unmistakable voices, Gramm’s powerful vocals helped define an era, fronting chart-topping hits like “I Want to Know What Love Is,” “Cold as Ice,” “Hot Blooded,” “Juke Box Hero,” and “Double Vision.”

Experience the timeless voice, the unforgettable songs, and the rock ’n’ roll spirit that continue to inspire generations.

This event, originally scheduled for Thursday, April 9, is now POSTPONED to Thursday, June 4. 
Often referred to as American Music Royalty, The Temptations are world-renowned superstars of entertainment, revered for their phenomenal catalog of music and prolific career.  Thanks to their fine-tuned choreography, and even finer harmonies, The Temptations became one of the most successful acts to record for Motown Records.  During the group’s six-decade career, these Grammy winners have charted numerous #1 hits including “My Girl,” “Ain’t Too Proud to Beg,” “Get Ready,” “Just My Imagination,” and “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone,” among many others. 
The Four Tops teamed up in high school and spent over four decades without a single personnel change to become one of Motown’s most consistent hit makers.  “Baby I Need Your Loving,” “I Can’t Help Myself (Sugar Pie, Honey Bunch),” “Reach Out (I’ll Be There),” “Standing in the Shadows of Love,” and “Ain’t No Woman (Like the One I’ve Got)” are just some of their classic hits.

title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
June 27, July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

Discover the amazing world of animals by looking at what’s inside! Animals with a sturdy backbone and a skeleton are called vertebrates, like leaping frogs, soaring birds, and even you.On the flip side, invertebrates are the "spineless" superstars of nature—like wiggly worms and crunchy beetles—who make up almost all the animals on Earth! location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $69 $79 $89 
 
If the phrase “male a cappella group” conjures up an image of students in blue blazers, ties, and khakis singing traditional college songs on ivied campuses… think again. Straight No Chaser (SNC) are neither strait-laced nor straight-faced, but neither are they vaudeville-style kitsch. They have emerged as a phenomenon with a massive fanbase and a long list of accomplishments including 2 RIAA Gold Certified albums, over 1.5 million concert tickets sold, over 1 billion streams on Pandora, and over 2 million albums sold worldwide. Straight No Chaser is the real deal, the captivating sound of nine unadulterated human voices coming together to make extraordinary music that is moving people in a fundamental sense… and with a sense of humor. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

Thousands of people come to the village of Bird-in-Hand for the auction which is held on the Smucker Homestead. Equine and antique enthusiasts, consignors, local residents, out-of-town visitors, and whole families look forward to our auction each year. title: Creative Release Open Studio Saturday
description:
The Creative House of Lancaster
#### ***A Place to Make Art Together***

**When:** Every Other Saturday from 10am - 12pm
**Where:** [The Candy Factory](https://share.google/nqC7VtCS6IcDeBRyg)
**Cost:** Free & Open to the Public
**Ages:** All Ages

**Upcoming Dates**
July 11, July 25, Aug 8, Aug 22, Sept 5, Sept 19, Oct 3, Oct 17, Oct 31, Nov 14, Nov 28, Dec 9, Dec 23

*Do you have creative aspirations but never seem to make the time? Do you want the companionship of others to overcome your creative blocks and “just do it”?*

Creative Release provides spaces and resources that make artmaking accessible. Whether you’re an experienced artist or just looking to explore your creative side, Creative Release is a safe place to explore your ideas with others. Bring your ongoing projects or use the art materials available.

Don't have a project at the moment? That's just fine. I’ll have materials to share.
**What to Expect:**

* A welcoming, inclusive environment
* A variety of art materials to experiment with
* Demonstrations on how to use different art materials
* The opportunity to work on your personal projects
* The chance to meet and collaborate with fellow creatives
* A moment to relax, create, and escape the usual routine

**Who Should Join?**
Anyone and everyone! Bring an idea for a card, a knitting pattern you’ve been wanting to try, a shirt that needs mending, or a full-on canvas and paints. Most of all, bring your lovely self! We believe in the power of community and creativity.

[Event Link](https://www.jodavis.art/community-events-1/creative-release)

location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:

AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, January 21 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, January 23 at 10:00 a.m. 
Legendary band, THREE DOG NIGHT, now in its 6th decade, claims some of the most astonishing statistics in popular music. In the years 1969 through 1974, no other group achieved more top 10 hits, moved more records, or sold more concert tickets than THREE DOG NIGHT. 
THREE DOG NIGHT hits weave through the fabric of pop culture today, whether on the radio where they are heard day in and day out, in TV commercials or in major motion pictures — songs like “Mama Told Me (Not To Come)”, “Joy to the World”, “Black and White”, “Shambala” and “One” serve to heighten our emotions and crystallize THREE DOG NIGHT’s continuing popularity. 
Boasting chart and sales records that remain virtually unmatched in popular music, THREE DOG NIGHT holds a Billboard Magazine record for releasing 21 consecutive Top 40 hits, including 3 #1 singles “Mama Told Me (Not to Come)”, “Joy to the World”, and “Liar; the chart success drove 7 Platinum-selling singles and 12 straight RIAA Certified Gold LPs. The hits appeared on best-selling charts in all genres (pop, rock, rhythm & blues, and country). Its records continue to sell around the world, reaching beyond the borders of the U.S. into Japan, Canada, Holland, England, Germany, Spain and elsewhere. Tens of millions of THREE DOG NIGHT records have been sold through the years. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Terry Fator Pure Imagination: Once Upon a Voice
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $49 $69 $79 $89
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, January 14 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, January 16 at 10:00 a.m. 
Legendary Las Vegas headliner Terry Fator has created a new road show to kickoff his 2025-2026 tour.  Pure Imagination: Once Upon a Voice is a 90 minute spectacular, featuring the incredible impressions, comedy and ventriloquism that has made Terry and his characters a must see show for fans across the nation. 
“Pure Imagination is a totally different concept than my road shows in the past,” Fator said. “I found that throughout my life my imagination had spawned countless characters, song parodies and comedy skits and I compiled them all together to give my audience a fun look into my creative psyche.” 
The show features the classic characters Terry has made famous over the years: Winston the Impersonating Turtle; Country Star Walter T. Airdale; Apollo Theater legend Julius; perpetual slacker and stoner Duggie; Vikki the Cougar and the world’s greatest Elvis impersonator, Maynard Tompkins. 
“One idea I had is to add in characters and impressions based on real-life stars people around the world know and love,” Fator said.  “So you can look forward to seeing and hearing Willie Nelson, Michael Jackson, Justin Bieber, plus a few surprise ‘guests’”. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: The Dolly Show: Kelly O'Brien - The World's #1 Dolly Parton Tribute
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $39 $49 $59
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, April 8 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, April 10 at 10:00 a.m. 
Experience the sparkle, heart, and unmistakable sound of country music’s most beloved icon with The Dolly Show: Kelly O’Brien – The World’s #1 Dolly Parton Tribute. 
If you can’t see Dolly Parton herself, Kelly O’Brien is the next best thing. Widely regarded as the most authentic and accomplished Dolly tribute artist in the world, Kelly has been personally endorsed by the Parton family and even selected by Dolly Parton Enterprises as Dolly’s official body double for film. She was also the only UK finalist in the global #SearchForDolly casting search for Dolly’s Broadway musical. 
More than a tribute, Kelly delivers a true illusion. With a pitch-perfect Tennessee accent, soaring soprano vocals, and the warmth, wit, and charm that define Dolly, she captures not just the look—but the spirit—of the Queen of Country. Audiences leave feeling uplifted, entertained, and convinced they’ve experienced something truly special. 
Backed by a live band, The Dolly Show is a dazzling, full-scale theatrical concert featuring Dolly’s greatest hits from the 1960s to today, including “Jolene,” “9 to 5,” “Islands in the Stream,” and “I Will Always Love You.” Expect powerhouse vocals, laugh-out-loud moments, rhinestone-studded glamour, and heartfelt storytelling throughout the evening. 
An award-winning performer with an international career spanning television, musical theatre, and live music, Kelly O’Brien has captivated audiences around the globe and appeared on major outlets including BBC One, ITV’s This Morning, Lorraine, Channel 5, and Sky. 
From the iconic silhouette to the signature Southern charm, Kelly O’Brien is Dolly—bringing one of music’s most treasured legends to life in a show that’s as joyful as it is unforgettable. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

location: Quarryville, QVL C.X. Carlson Cultural Room
description:

Adults and interested older children. Please register each person in your group.The land we today call Lancaster County has a rich history that stretches millennia into the past. Archaeology has given us a unique toolset to peer into this deep past and glimpse the lives of the earliest peoples to live on this land, who have been hunting, gardening, engineering, philosophizing, crafting, dancing, playing, and much more for countless generations. This presentation will focus on pre-European contact and early contact archaeological sites and theories to paint a picture of what life may have been like for some of the various Indigenous peoples who inhabited and shaped this region in the past.

Aaron Lewis, the Vermont-born powerhouse first found success with Staind–the 2000s-era hard-rockers who injected meditative muscle into an era better known for mindless aggression. But while that band is still very much alive, it was never enough to satisfy Lewis’ creative drive. 
Embracing his roots to earn a rare second round of success, a series of solo country projects have led to two No. 1 Billboard Country Album debuts–TOWN LINE (2011) and SINNER(2016)–plus a PLATINUM collab with heroes George Jones and Charlie Daniels (“Country Boy”), and a GOLD-certified Billboard No. 1 with “Am I The Only One” in 2021. Lewis’ 2022 solo album followed suit, with FRAYED AT BOTH ENDS emerging as the best-selling Country album in America but he never wrote songs for the stats. No matter the sonic setting, Lewis writes andsings to get his truth out and his latest album THE HILL(2024) is no different.

description:

Patty Griffin, a two-time GRAMMY® Award winner and one of the most influential singer-songwriters of her generation, brings her deeply personal and emotionally rich music to the stage. Celebrated for her masterful storytelling and soulful voice, Griffin has spent over two decades crafting songs that explore love, loss, identity, and the shared experiences that connect us all. 
Blending folk, Americana, and blues, her music resonates with honesty and depth. Her latest album, Crown of Roses, is an intimate and introspective collection born from a period of reflection, offering songs that speak to resilience, transformation, and embracing new truths. Experience an evening with an artist whose songs linger long after the final note. 
Kathleen Edwards is a modern-day cornerstone of North American roots music. Since making her debut with 2002’s Failer, she’s spent the 21st century occupying the grey area between genres, swirling together her own mix of alt-country, folk, and heartland rock & roll. It’s a sound that has earned its creator more than a half-dozen Juno nominations, shows with icons like Bob Dylan and Willie Nelson, and Top 40 success on both sides of the Canadian/American border. From co-writes with Maren Morris to critically-acclaimed solo records like Back to Me, Asking for Flowers, Voyageur, and Total Freedom, Edwards has become a leader of the Americana community, even as her ever-evolving music reaches beyond the format’s boundaries.

Relive the soundtrack of a generation when Tommy James & The Shondells take the stage for a night of nonstop hits and pure nostalgia. With an incredible string of chart-topping classics, this legendary group helped define the sound of the late ’60s and early ’70s — and their music continues to ignite audiences around the world. 
Sing along to iconic favorites like “Crimson and Clover,” “Mony Mony,” “I Think We’re Alone Now,” “Hanky Panky,” and “Mirage.” Packed with unforgettable melodies, driving rhythms, and timeless pop-rock energy, this concert delivers hit after hit in a high-octane live performance that spans decades of musical history. 
Whether you grew up with these songs on the radio or discovered them through movies, commercials, and modern covers, Tommy James & The Shondells bring a feel-good evening of classic rock that’s perfect for fans of all ages. Don’t miss your chance to experience these legendary songs performed live — a night of memories, music, and pure fun awaits.

title: The Beach Boys: Saluting 60 Years of Pet Sounds
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $59 $79 $99 $119
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Thursday, February 26 at 9:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, February 27 at 10:00 a.m. 
  
As The Beach Boys mark more than a half century of making music, the group continues to ride the crest of a wave unequalled in America’s musical history. The Beach Boys – who have become synonymous with the California lifestyle and an American icon to fans around the world – are bringing “The Sounds of Summer” tour to cities around the globe. 
Since the band’s co-founder, lead-singer and chief lyricist Mike Love penned the lyrics to The Beach Boys’ first hit,“Surfin’” (1961), dozens of the bands chart toppers have become eternal anthems of American youth: “Surfin’ USA,” “Surfer Girl,” “Fun, Fun, Fun,” “I Get Around,” “California Girls,” “Help Me Rhonda,” “Barbara Ann,” “Good Vibrations,” “Wouldn’t It Be Nice,” “Rock and Roll Music” and “Kokomo.” 
The Beach Boys have sold over 100 million records worldwide and have received more than 33 RIAA Platinum and Gold record awards. The Rock And Roll Hall of Famers where also honored at the 2001 Grammy Awards with the Lifetime Achievement Award. With more than five decades of touring under their belts, The Beach Boys have performed more concerts than any major rock band in history. 
The Beach Boys are led by legendary Rock and Roll Hall of Fame inductee, Grammy® winner, New York Times best-selling author, co-founder, lead singer, chief lyricist of The Beach Boys, and 2025 Songwriters Hall of Fame inductee, Mike Love, who, along with musical director Brian Eichenberger, Christian Love, Tim Bonhomme, Jon Bolton, Keith Hubacher, Randy Leago and John Wedemeyer continue the legacy of the iconic band. 
In 2026, The Beach Boys are celebrating 250 years of the USA while saluting The 60th Anniversary of Pet Sounds.

title: Oh Captain My Captain! For Tweens
location: Ephrata, EPH 1/2 Multipurpose Room Kitchen Side
description:
Gaming, Tweens

Oh Captain, My Captain! is a short form world-building role-playing game (RPG) that explores heroism and the complicated relationships we have with people we admire. The game revolves around players drawing from a deck of cards with open-ended questions. Each question players answer helps them learn about their character, their world, their captain and the complicated relationship they have with a living legend. Players use these answers to make connections between their stories leading up one of three final questions that end the game. No experience or prep needed! Ages 10-12.

description:

Book selections are chosen by teens during advisory meetings. Interested in joining the Teen Advisory Board? Sign up through the library calendar. Each month, we’ll dive into a new title—ranging from trending young adult fiction to graphic novels, fantasy epics, thought-provoking contemporary stories, and more.This month we'll be reading "Sumer of Broken Rules" by K.L. Walther. You’ll get the chance to share your thoughts, hear different perspectives, and connect with fellow book lovers in a relaxed and welcoming space. Snacks will be provided, and occasionally we’ll have themed activities or giveaways tied to the book!Note: To help everyone stay present and get the most out of the experience, we ask that all phones stay in pockets or bags during the program. title: Jeremy Camp
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $39 $59 $69 $79
AMT Member Pre-Sale: Wednesday, April 8 at 10:00 a.m.
Public On-Sale: Friday, April 10 at 10:00 a.m. 
Spend an inspiring evening with Jeremy Camp, one of contemporary Christian music’s most influential and enduring artists. Known for his powerful blend of worship and rock, Camp has spent more than two decades creating music that connects deeply with audiences through messages of hope, perseverance, and faith. 
With chart-topping songs like “I Still Believe,” “Walk by Faith,” and “There Will Be a Day,” his live performances are both uplifting and deeply personal—bringing together heartfelt storytelling and dynamic musicianship. 
Camp’s impact on Christian music has earned him widespread recognition, including multiple GMA Dove Awards—with wins for New Artist of the Year and Male Vocalist of the Year—along with numerous additional nominations across his career. He has also received American Music Award nominations for Favorite Contemporary Inspirational Artist and a Grammy Award nomination for Best Pop/Contemporary Gospel Album. 
Backed by a talented band and delivered with authenticity, this concert offers an evening of meaningful music and connection. Whether you’ve followed his career for years or are discovering his music for the first time, Jeremy Camp’s live performance is an experience that leaves a lasting impression. 
For certain concerts, audience members may prefer to stand or dance, especially when encouraged by the artist to do so. Guest expectations differ, so we simply ask all attendees to extend mutual respect toward one another and maintain awareness of those around them. Our staff will only intervene in matters of safety or when behavior is deemed unruly, combative, or disruptive to the overall performance.

title: Ben & Rose with Conrad Fisher
location: American Music Theatre, 2425 Lincoln Hwy East, Lancaster, PA, 17605, United States
description:
Tickets: $29 $34 $39 
Ben & Rose are more than just a duo — they’re a harmony born of Lancaster County’s Plain Community, where tradition, faith, and family shape every note. Their music carries the quiet strength of country roads and the timeless beauty of rural life, weaving humility and heart into every song. Blending country, folk, and gospel, Ben & Rose create music that is both tender and timeless. Their young voices lock together like old friends, evoking front-porch evenings, Sunday hymns, and the kind of stories that linger long after the last note. Each performance is a reminder that simple living can yield the richest music — songs filled with love, hope, and the rhythms of everyday grace. 
Their journey began as teenagers singing side by side, finding harmonies to Lady Antebellum tracks at local youth gatherings. What started at karaoke nights grew into something far deeper: a loving marriage and a shared passion for storytelling through song. Today, their harmonies carry the same spark of those early days, polished by years of life, love, and laughter together. 
Ben & Rose often collaborate with fellow Plain Community songwriter Conrad Fisher, whose work has been recorded by legends like the Oak Ridge Boys, Rhonda Vincent, and The Malpass Brothers. Together, they craft music that feels both rooted and refreshing — a modern echo of simpler times, celebrating the beauty found in everyday life.

title: Bird-in-Hand Hot Air Balloon Festival
location: Bird-in-Hand Event Field, 320 North Ronks Road, Bird-in-Hand, 17505, United States
description:
We’re taking our favorite high-flying, family-friendly fun fall event to new heights! 
We’re thrilled to partner with Balloon Shows USA to bring you an all-new balloon festival. Enjoy a weekend of spectacular hot air balloon glows and laser light shows, music, family activities, food trucks, craft vendors and more. 
You’ll find lots to do in the afternoon and evening. Ascend in a tethered balloon, weather permitting. Browse our retailers’ offerings. If you’re bringing little ones, take a wagon ride, visit our kids’ area, and let them burn off some energy in the bounce houses. Grab a bite to eat from our food trucks; each will offer a special bacon-themed dish in addition to its regular menu. 
At 8:30, the lights come on and the fun kicks into high gear. Watch as massive tethered hot air balloons illuminate the night and state-of-the-art laser displays paint the sky with brilliant colors. It’s an unforgettable sight and an experience you won’t want to miss. 
What to expect: 

Massive balloons and special shaped balloons guaranteed to delight kids and adults alike.
Check your bucket list and get a ride in a real tethered balloon ($35, weather permitting).
High-energy entertainment all evening with our DJ.
Shop, explore and discover craft and retail vendors with unique finds and handmade goods.
Satisfy your cravings at our food truck festival, featuring special bacon-themed creations from select vendors.
Take in the scenery and enjoy our farm with free hayrides.
Don’t miss the Kids Zone with games, rides, bounce houses and nonstop fun ($5 to $20 for unlimited rides).
The Grand Finale (8:30 pm nightly) with Balloon Glow & Laser Show, music and synchronized balloon burn, giant glowing balloons and crowd countdowns

Dates: Friday, September 25, 2026 & Saturday, September 26, 2026
Time: 3 pm–10 pm both days
Grand Finale: 8:30 pm 
Tickets:  
In advance
VIP: $45/day
Adults: $25/day
Kids (6-12): $15/day
Kids (5 and under): FREE 
Tickets will be available at the gate for an additional cost. 
Get tickets now before we sell out. 
Click here to order tickets

title: Free with Admission: Chemistry Magic with Eurofins Lancaster Labs
location: The Lancaster Science Factory, 454 New Holland Ave, Lancaster, PA, 17602, United States
description:
Come one come all to the Chemistry Magic Show presented by real scientists from Eurofins Lancaster Laboratories! 
This dazzling show incorporates a variety of experiments to ignite your mind from homemade rocket fuel to disappearing cups, to color-changing bottles and so much more! All ages are encouraged to participate in these hands-on experiments and watch the fascinating chemical reactions. 
This activity is FREE with your paid admission or membership to the Lancaster Science Factory.
